ruleName: Restrictions on Touching Sand in Bunker
imagePrompt: A modern semi-realistic (75% realistic, 25% stylised) illustration in a clear, polished junior golf quiz style. Show a bunker on a golf course with a green in the background. A golfer is in the bunker, having just lost their balance, and their hand is on the sand near their ball. The ball is lying clearly on the bunker sand several feet from the player's hand. It must be obvious that the contact is accidental (such as through body posture suggesting recovering balance). The player’s club is not touching the sand. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer in a bunker has accidentally touched the sand with their hand near their ball while regaining balance. The golf ball is lying on the sand in the bunker, and the player appears to have made accidental contact rather than testing the sand.

sceneSpec.setting: Bunker on a golf course, with a green visible in the background.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer in the bunker, appearing to have just lost balance, with their hand touching the sand beside the ball.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: The ball is lying on the sand inside the bunker, several feet in front of the player’s hand.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: Player has just accidentally touched the sand with their hand while walking to address their ball.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Demonstrates the Rules related to accidental touching of sand in a bunker when not improving conditions affecting the stroke.
mustShow: Golf ball lying in the bunker sand
Golfer with one hand touching the sand near the ball in a way that clearly indicates loss of balance or an accidental touch
Player not holding a club against the sand
mustNotShow: Grounding a club in front of or behind the ball
Any signs of deliberate improving of the sand
Text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles

questions.title: Oops! I Touched the Sand in the Bunker
questions.question: Your ball is in a bunker (the sandy place). As you walk to your ball, you slip and your hand touches the sand next to your ball by accident. What happens now?

choices.text: You get a big penalty because you touched the sand in the bunker.
You get a one-shot penalty for touching the sand before hitting your ball.
You do not get a penalty because it was an accident and you did not make things better for your next shot.
You have to rake the sand before you hit your shot.

questions.explanation: You don’t get a penalty if you touch the sand by accident, like if you slipped or lost balance. You only get a penalty if you touch the sand to make it easier for your swing or to test it. Just be careful not to change the sand to help your shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A bunker is a special sandy area on the golf course. If your ball lands here, it is harder to hit.
A penalty means you add extra shots to your score for breaking a rule.

questions.teachingTip: Let children practise standing safely in bunkers and talk them through what is and isn’t allowed before they swing.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think any touch of sand is a penalty, but it only matters if it helps your next shot or if you do it on purpose.
Some might believe they have to rake every time before hitting – raking is for after your shot.

questions.title: Accidentally Touching the Sand in a Bunker
questions.question: Your ball is in a bunker. As you walk towards it, you accidentally lose your balance and your hand touches the sand beside your ball. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: You receive the general penalty because you touched the sand in the bunker.
You receive a one-stroke penalty because you touched the sand before making a stroke.
There is no penalty because the contact with the sand was accidental and did not improve the conditions affecting your stroke.
You must rake the area before playing your shot.

questions.explanation: The Rules no longer prohibit every contact with the sand in a bunker. There is no penalty if you accidentally touch the sand, such as keeping your balance, entering or leaving the bunker, or placing your clubs in the bunker, provided you do not improve the conditions affecting your stroke. Penalty only applies if you deliberately touch the sand to test its condition, or improve conditions affecting your stroke. Rule Reference: Rule 12.2b.
